name: DCT Sollers
author: doblejou

sections.description:
DCT Sollers brings five independent modules to Settings → DCT Sollers. Enable only what you need. Each module has its own tab, accessible even when the module is off, and disabling a module preserves its settings and data.

  • Login protection: Limits failed sign-in attempts per IP, temporarily blocks access to wp-login.php, and lets administrators review active blocks and unblock individual IPs. Enabled by default.
  • CLI migration: Exports and imports single-site installations in the plugin’s own ZIP format. Run commands in WP-CLI; the admin tab shows instructions only. Enabled by default.
  • CDN: Rewrites eligible local asset URLs to your existing CDN hostname. Choose file extensions and exclusions without changing stored URLs or files. Disabled by default.
  • Frontend: Choose which WordPress-generated tags and assets to remove, which hosts to connect to early, and which WOFF2 fonts or front-page image to preload. Disabled by default; all settings start off or empty.
  • Comments: Disable public comments site-wide or by post type, without deleting existing comments or disabling private editor notes. Disabled by default.

The Comments module closes native submissions, including through REST and XML-RPC, and incoming pingbacks and trackbacks for affected posts. It hides their existing comments from native public views, comment feeds, and public REST reads. WooCommerce products are left alone unless explicitly selected; stored ratings are not recalculated. Existing comments remain available for authorized moderation. Purge page caches after changing the policy. Custom comment systems and endpoints may require separate configuration.

The plugin uses native WordPress APIs without requiring an external PHP library or a commercial service. WordPress Multisite is not supported.

Login protection and privacy

Defaults: 3 failed attempts within a rolling 1-minute window trigger a 15-minute block. The threshold, time window, and block duration are configurable. Further requests do not extend a block, and changing the settings does not change when existing blocks expire. REST, XML-RPC, and external authentication forms are not protected.

IP addresses and timestamps for failed attempts and blocks are stored locally, without credentials. Hourly cleanup removes expired records and depends on WP-Cron. Blocks expire on time even if cleanup is delayed. Shared IP addresses share their attempt counter and block.

The IP address comes exclusively from REMOTE_ADDR. When using a proxy or CDN, configure the server to resolve the real visitor IP correctly; the plugin does not interpret proxy headers. Site operators should disclose this processing in their privacy policy and determine its legal basis.

Migration through WP-CLI

Export from the source site, then run the import commands from the destination site, with WordPress and DCT Sollers already installed. Start with --dry-run to validate the package and review the plan without changing destination files or tables. Database rows are checked against foreign key constraints during the actual import, not during the dry run.

wp dct-sollers export --file=/ruta/privada/sitio.zip
wp dct-sollers import --file=/ruta/privada/sitio-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.zip --mode=merge --dry-run
wp dct-sollers import --file=/ruta/privada/sitio-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.zip --mode=merge
wp dct-sollers import --file=/ruta/privada/sitio-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.zip --mode=mirror

Export appends a random 32-character hexadecimal identifier to the filename and prints the final path. Use that path on the destination, or the private path where you transferred the ZIP. Exported archives and import packages are not deleted automatically.

Importing overwrites data, users, and code. It does not create a backup or guarantee rollback. Make an independent backup before importing and only use trusted packages. Packages contain unencrypted sensitive data: store them outside public directories with restricted access.

Both modes replace included tables in full and overwrite matching files. merge keeps additional files and tables; mirror removes them within the migration scope. Exclusions are preserved. The destination keeps its existing public and WordPress URLs unless you specify --home-url or --site-url. WordPress core, wp-config.php, and server configuration are not migrated. The ZIP format is not compatible with .wpress.

For a live import, WP-CLI first prints an isolated startup command using --exec and stops before changing the site. Run the printed command yourself. After the data is imported, run the full finalization command it prints. Maintenance mode stays on until verification and cache cleanup succeed. Do not start another migration between those steps. If a live import fails after changes begin, the site may be left partially restored and in maintenance mode.

Migration requires WP-CLI, 64-bit PHP, ZipArchive, mysqli, and InnoDB tables. Custom local content paths are supported, but overlapping roots, multiple theme roots, path collisions, symbolic links, views, triggers, and partitioned tables are not. Use an absolute export path in an existing private directory. Export never overwrites an existing ZIP; do not use an archive left behind by an interrupted export.

CDN and external connections

The administrator must configure a CDN separately. The plugin does not configure providers, upload files, or purge caches. It rewrites resources in public HTML and content.rendered and excerpt.rendered fields for REST post types, not arbitrary JSON or external CSS/JS files.

When this module is enabled, visitors request rewritten resources from the selected CDN hostname. Its provider may receive visitor IP addresses and the usual HTTP request data. Review the provider’s terms and privacy policy before configuring the hostname.

Saving settings makes no external requests. The Check CDN button explicitly sends a HEAD request to the saved hostname at wp-includes/images/blank.gif, with the site origin as Referer and without following redirects. HTTP 200 does not certify all resources or their CORS headers. Fonts require appropriate CORS configuration at the CDN/origin. Invalidate page caches after changing module settings or status. Do not use this module simultaneously with CDN Enabler.

Frontend optimization and external connections

Cleanup options cover emoji compatibility assets, RSD links, shortlinks, Dashicons for logged-out visitors, REST and oEmbed discovery, the HTML generator tag, and separate RSS discovery controls for content and comments. Each option explains what it removes and what stays available. Removing discovery links does not disable the corresponding endpoints or feeds. Removing the HTML generator tag is cosmetic, not a security measure.

Frontend uses native WordPress resource-hint and preload APIs. Configure up to 10 HTTP(S) preconnect origins, 10 DNS-prefetch hostnames, 5 absolute WOFF2 font URLs and one absolute image URL for the non-paginated front page. Fonts use anonymous CORS. Do not preload unnecessary resources: this can make performance worse. Visitor Dashicons cleanup may affect theme icons; dependency styles can still require Dashicons.

No resources are downloaded by the server. Configured hints and preloads may cause visitors’ browsers to connect to third parties before those resources are used. Use trusted destinations consistent with your privacy and consent policy. No third-party destinations are configured automatically. Match actual theme/CDN resource URLs, including query parameters, and invalidate page caches after changes. CDN HTML rewriting also applies to eligible preload URLs. The module does not generate critical CSS, defer scripts globally, or remove other plugins’ assets automatically.
sections.installation:
1. Search for DCT Sollers under Plugins → Add Plugin, or upload the ZIP from that screen.
  2. Activate DCT Sollers.
  3. Open Settings → DCT Sollers and configure the modules you need.
  4. Before enabling CDN rewriting, configure its hostname and verify the service and CORS.

To update, use WordPress’s plugin updater or replace the plugin files without uninstalling. Deactivation preserves data; uninstalling removes the IP table, plugin settings, and scheduled cleanup event. Exported ZIP files are not deleted on uninstall.
sections.faq:
How can I unblock an administrator?

From another IP address, use Settings → DCT Sollers → Login protection. Alternatively, use WP-CLI:

wp eval 'DCTSollers_Store::unlock("192.0.2.10");'

Does this replace a firewall?

No. Protection is IP-based and limited to wp-login.php. It does not replace server-side protection or a WAF against distributed attacks.

Can I run a migration from a browser?

No. The migration tab only displays instructions; exporting and importing require WP-CLI.

Can I switch from DCT WP Hero or an older build that uses a different internal prefix?

DCT Sollers does not import settings, blocks, scheduled events, or migration packages from DCT WP Hero or builds with earlier internal prefixes. Make a separate backup, deactivate the old plugin, and configure DCT Sollers again. Do not run both plugins together. The CLI command is wp dct-sollers.
sections.changelog:
0.3.1

  • Standardized headings, notices, and save buttons across module settings screens.

0.3.0

  • Added the optional, reversible Comments module with global or per-post-type control, private editor note support, and opt-in closure for WooCommerce products.

0.2.27

  • Add a cryptographically random 128-bit identifier to exported archive filenames and display the final local path for imports.
  • Retain private archive storage, 0600 permissions and temporary-file cleanup; exported archives remain under operator control.

0.2.26

  • Require explicit operator-run migration startup and finalization without launching programs from PHP.
  • Publish verified private exports without hard links or overwriting existing files.
  • Use WordPress filesystem APIs for migration deletions and identify persistent maintenance per import.
  • Remove only the matching maintenance file after verification and cache cleanup, without evaluating its contents.
  • Centralize plugin paths and URLs using WordPress directory functions.
  • Reject package entries that collide with customized destination roots before any site writes.
  • Support unconditional mu-plugin directory definitions during isolated configuration loading without hiding unrelated diagnostics.
  • Translate module labels only for presentation after init, avoiding early translation-loading notices.

0.2.25

  • Maintenance release for directory review; enable WordPress debugging throughout the disposable test suites.

0.2.24

  • Resolve customized local migration directories and preserve destination uploads settings.
  • Load the ABSPATH-protected import worker through native WP-CLI isolation startup.
  • Make Settings API sanitization explicit at registration.
  • Switch all internal identifiers to dctsollers without compatibility with previous data or packages.

0.2.23

  • Group each Frontend cleanup option’s explanations in its own collapsed accordion while keeping checkboxes visible.

0.2.22

  • Package the current development changes for distribution.

0.2.21

  • Establish independent settings, storage and CLI commands for the Sollers plugin.
  • Install separately without importing previous plugin settings, login blocks or migration archives.
  • Document narrowly scoped CLI diagnostic exceptions and test that URL conflicts identify the relevant configuration constant.

0.2.20

  • Move login storage initialization and scheduled cleanup into module lifecycle callbacks.
  • Separate login and CDN settings into dedicated classes with consistent defaults, validation and read methods.
  • Split migration destination resolution, planning and file restoration from CLI coordination while preserving safety checks.
  • Add independent module test runners using shared disposable-site infrastructure.

0.2.19

  • Redesigned the administration interface with responsive module cards, clearer navigation and visible saved module states.
  • Added scoped, dependency-free CSS loaded only on the plugin settings screen, without custom JavaScript.
  • Improved keyboard focus, narrow-screen tables and cleanup option layout while preserving visible help.
  • Removed duplicate HTML identifiers from CDN and IP unlock forms without changing nonce protection.

0.2.18

  • Added independent REST/oEmbed discovery, HTML generator and content/comment RSS discovery cleanup options, all off by default.
  • Added visible explanations of what each cleanup removes, preserves and may affect, with accessible help for every checkbox.
  • Preserve existing settings when adding the new cleanup options and keep REST, oEmbed and feed endpoints available.
  • Prefix frontend template variables and document narrowly scoped Plugin Check false positives.

0.2.17

  • Added the optional Frontend module with emoji, RSD, shortlink and visitor Dashicons cleanup.
  • Added configurable preconnect, DNS prefetch, WOFF2 font preloads and a front-page image preload using native WordPress APIs.
  • Added frontend settings validation and HTTP integration tests, including CDN rewriting, permissions and persistence.

0.2.16

  • Validate DOCUMENT_ROOT types during export while preserving WP-CLI support for absent or empty values.
  • Prefix migration finalization and verification helper variables.

0.2.15

  • Added author and contributor metadata.
  • Use WordPress-compatible writable checks during migration.
  • Escape control characters in CLI diagnostics without HTML-encoding terminal output.
  • Document scoped SQL, streaming, filesystem, and early-bootstrap review exceptions.

0.2.14

  • Metadata and documentation preparation for the WordPress directory.
  • Translator comments, read-only admin navigation handling, and prefixed template variables.
  • WordPress URL parsing and explicit WordPress/CLI guards for migration helper scripts.

0.2.13

  • Login protection, CLI migration, and CDN modules.

screenshots.caption: Modules: enable or disable each tool independently and see its saved status.
Login protection: configure the threshold, time window, and block duration, and manage active IP blocks.
CLI migration: see export, validation, import, and finalization instructions.
CDN: set the hostname, file extensions, and exclusions, and check the saved configuration.
Frontend: choose cleanup options and configure resource hints and preloads.
